messages:
ben: hey team, ben here (day 2). Followed the onboarding steps but I'm getting tripped up by kubeconfig merging. I have three contexts and the onboarding doc mentions `redwood-dev`. I can switch to it but it doesn't default to my namespace `team-ben`. Who do I ask to set a namespace alias or RBAC?
tara-infra: welcome Ben! We handle RoleBindings. For the namespace default you can run `kubectl config set-context redwood-dev --namespace=team-ben` locally. If your context is missing entirely, run `gcloud container clusters get-credentials redwood-dev --zone us-central1-a --project redwood-prod` (GKE) or `aws eks update-kubeconfig` for EKS. Which cloud are you on?
ben: using GKE. Did the get-credentials step, context present, `kubectl config use-context redwood-dev` works but `kubectl get pods` fails with "forbidden" when I don't specify -n team-ben.
dotbot: created ticket ONB-3321 for ben: request RoleBinding in namespace team-ben. Assigned to tara-infra.
tara-infra: you likely need a RoleBinding. Are you joining as contractor or employee? We bind different groups. Also paste `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-ben`.
ben: employee. `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-ben` -> no. SSO email ben@redwood.ai. My `kubectl config view --minify --flatten` shows an extra user entry from personal cluster with an `auth-provider` that looks stale. Could that matter?
tara-infra: yes stale users can confuse the auth plugin. Two steps: 1) I'll create a RoleBinding `rb-ben-onboard` in team-ben binding group `redwood-developers-onboard` for your SSO. 2) locally remove old user entries or run `kubectl config view --minify --flatten > ~/.kube/config` to produce a clean config after the cloud credential step.
eli-eng: another tip: if you want to avoid changing configs, create a context alias: `kubectl config rename-context gke_redwood redwood-dev` or `kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=team-ben` once you're on the redwood-dev context. Saves typing `-n`.
tara-infra: RoleBinding created: `rb-ben-onboard` in `team-ben`. Wait ~20s and try `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-ben` then `kubectl get pods -n team-ben`. If you still see Unauthorized, run `gcloud auth login --brief` and re-run get-credentials.
ben: after ~30s `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-ben` -> yes. `kubectl get pods -n team-ben` -> No resources found. Set default namespace with `kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=team-ben` and it's smooth now. Thanks!
security-bryan: quick reminder on secrets: if you need read access to secrets in your namespace, open a secrets request and include why + TTL. We prefer short-lived access during onboarding.
ben: noted, will file if I need secrets. Really appreciated the fast turnaround :thumbsup:
